text: Tides are the regular rise and fall of sea level, caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun acting on the rotating Earth, and they shape coastlines everywhere.
label: content

text: The Moon's gravity pulls on the ocean nearest to it, creating a bulge of water. A second bulge forms on the opposite side, because the Earth itself is pulled toward the Moon more strongly than the distant water.
label: content

text: As the Earth rotates through these bulges, most coastlines experience two high tides and two low tides every lunar day, which lasts about twenty-four hours and fifty minutes.
label: content

text: Spring tides happen when the Sun and Moon align, producing larger ranges.
label: content

text: Neap tides happen when they are at right angles, producing smaller ranges.
